ORNL's Fuels Engines and Emissions Research Center develops advanced catalyst technologies to control vehicle emissions of unburned fuel, nitrogen oxides and particulates, like soot. In this picture, slender glass tubes inserted into two channels of a catalytic converter take samples of exhaust gases. This sort of sampling, combined with advanced analytical techniques, enables researchers to study the chemistry of vehicle exhaust as it moves through the converter. This technology was used to optimize emissions from the groundbreaking 2007 Dodge Ram heavy-duty pickup truck, which met 2010 emissions control standards three years ahead of schedule.
